question:
A clinical study is studying new genetic gene-based therapies for children and adults with sickle cell disease. The patients were informed that they were divided into two age groups since younger patients suffer from different complications of the disease. The pediatric group is more likely to suffer from which of the complications?
I. Splenic sequestration
II. Avascular necrosis
III. Pulmonary hypertension
IV. Acute chest syndrome
V. Nephropathy?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pediatric patients with sickle cell disease" -> "higher risk of splenic sequestration" -> "due to smaller spleen size and function" -> "more likely to experience acute complications" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Pediatric patients with sickle cell disease" -> "increased incidence of acute chest syndrome" -> "due to frequent infections and vaso-occlusive crises" -> "more common in younger age group" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Pediatric patients with sickle cell disease" -> "less likely to experience avascular necrosis" -> "as this complication is more common in older patients" -> "due to cumulative damage over time" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Pediatric patients with sickle cell disease" -> "higher risk of nephropathy" -> "but this is more common in adults" -> "therefore less likely in pediatric group" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Pediatric patients with sickle cell disease" -> "more likely to suffer from splenic sequestration" -> "and acute chest syndrome" -> "due to age-related complications" -> 90%
analysis: In children with sickle cell disease, splenic sequestration and acute chest syndrome are more common complications. Splenic sequestration occurs due to the trapping of sickled red blood cells in the spleen, leading to splenic enlargement and potential hypovolemic shock. Acute chest syndrome, characterized by chest pain, fever, and respiratory symptoms, is also more prevalent in pediatric patients. Avascular necrosis, pulmonary hypertension, and nephropathy are more commonly seen in adults. Therefore, the pediatric group is more likely to suffer from complications I and IV.
